rules.quote: When writing official dual names, use a spaced forward slash to separate the 2 parts of the name.

when: When writing official dual names of places.

rules.quote: Use capitals for names of places, roads and streets

when: Applies to names of places, roads, streets, and other thoroughfares (including topographic features).

rules.quote: Do not add punctuation marks to these.
rules.violation_condition: punctuation marks (such as full stops) added to abbreviations or contractions in an address
when: Applies to abbreviations and contractions used in addresses.
rules.why: G-4: actionable prohibition against punctuate abbreviations in addresses.

covers.quote: The last line should contain the place name or post office of delivery, state or territory abbreviation and postcode.

examples.note: Last line in all capitals, no punctuation, postcode last.

rules.quote: When addressing a letter, write the last line in capitals without punctuation or underlining, with the postcode last.
rules.violation_condition: the last line of an address on a letter written with lower-case letters, punctuation marks, underlining, or without the postcode placed last
when: When addressing a letter for Australian domestic delivery.
rules.why: G-2: specific rule on formatting the destination line of an addressed letter.

rules.quote: If you are sending mail overseas, spell out all names in the address in full to avoid confusion.
rules.violation_condition: abbreviated place, state, or country names in an overseas mail address
when: When sending mail overseas.
rules.why: G-2: specific exception/condition for international mail addressing.

parts.quote: St Paul’s Cathedral is close to Melbourne’s Federation Square. The cathedral ...

rules.quote: Names of buildings, structures and public places have initial capitals. Write generic and plural terms in lower case.
rules.violation_condition: a building, structure, or public place name written in lower case, or generic/plural terms written with initial capitals
when: When naming buildings, structures, and public places.
Generic and plural terms (e.g. 'the cathedral', 'bridges') take lower case.
rules.why: G-4: combines heading rule and body specification on generic/plural terms.

rules.quote: Use initial capitals for the names of private properties.
rules.violation_condition: a private property name written without initial capitals
when: When writing the names of private properties (e.g. stations, downs, homesteads).
rules.why: G-2: distinct rule covering private properties.

covers.quote: Shorten names for states and territories in 4 situations
You can use shortened forms when:
the name is used as an adjective
space is limited
the full name would result in repetition
you are writing an address.

parts.quote: The WA Government has reopened the Eyre Highway.

rules.quote: Spell out the names of Australian states and territories in formal content.
rules.specification: Use the full name of states and territories unless used as an adjective, space is limited, repeating the full name, or writing an address.
rules.violation_condition: shortened forms of Australian state or territory names used in formal content where none of the permitted conditions apply
when: In formal content.
Shortened forms are permitted when: the name is used as an adjective, space is limited, the full name would result in repetition, or you are writing an address.
rules.why: G-2, G-3: default rule is to spell out, with 4 permitted exceptions.

covers.quote: This rule applies to the initialisms (NSW, WA, ACT and NT), abbreviations (Vic and Tas) and the contraction (Qld).

rules.quote: Don’t use a full stop after the shortened forms.
rules.violation_condition: a full stop following an abbreviation, initialism, or contraction of an Australian state or territory (e.g. 'Vic.', 'Qld.', 'N.S.W.')
when: Applies to all shortened forms of Australian states and territories (NSW, WA, ACT, NT, Vic, Tas, Qld, SA).
rules.why: G-2: specific punctuation prohibition on shortened state/territory forms.
